entities.name: Ronald Reagan
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ronald Wilson Reagan (1911–2004) was the 40th President of the United States (1981–1989), a former Hollywood actor who became the most consequential conservative leader of the 20th century. His presidency restored American confidence after the malaise of the 1970s, launched the neoliberal revolution, and—through massive military buildup and rhetorical confrontation—helped bring about the end of the Cold War.

Reagan won the 1980 election in a landslide against Jimmy Carter, promising to cut taxes, reduce government, and confront the Soviet Union. His supply-side 'Reaganomics'—combining large tax cuts with increased military spending—reduced inflation but tripled the national debt. He survived an assassination attempt in 1981, quipping to surgeons: 'I hope you're all Republicans.'

His 1987 speech at the Berlin Wall—'Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!'—became the defining moment of his presidency. The Strategic Defence Initiative ('Star Wars'), his arms buildup, and his willingness to negotiate with Gorbachev at Reykjavik (1986) are credited by many historians with hastening the Soviet collapse.

Reagan left office with the highest approval rating since FDR. The Iran-Contra affair and deregulation's long-term consequences remain controversial. He was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in 1994 and died in 2004. He transformed the Republican Party and American conservatism in ways that persist to this day.
